clue.text: Memorial's significance delved into by character abroad

indicators.note: something delved into is dug open, so the first word is cut open by the second

parts.note: a matter of moment is one of significance
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign character

explanation.surface: A memorial's meaning is being investigated by some foreign figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Memorial's' is read as 'Memorial is', the definition plus a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument is a structure erected to commemorate someone, a synonym for memorial.

clue.text: Pastime mostly having appeal for little creature with hairy feet

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a hobby is a pastime
IT is sex appeal, as in an 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A small hairy-footed being enjoys a hobby that is somewhat attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's halflings are small creatures described as having hairy, leathery-soled feet.

clue.text: End of garden rake used first in French port

indicators.note: says the rake's letters come before the garden's end in the answer

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a roué

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A gardener in a French harbour town puts the rake to use before finishing the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' looks like a garden tool, but here it is the old word for a libertine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouen is a port on the Seine in Normandy, France.

clue.text: Eulogistic article penned by archbishop, one with right-wing views

indicators.note: the article is written by the archbishop, so his name comes first, like an author's byline

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I
a is the indefinite article
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: An archbishop writes a flattering piece about a right-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: LAUD is William Laud, Archbishop of Canterbury executed in 1645.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudatory means full of praise, which is what eulogistic describes.

clue.text: Merciless cutting back by a Parisian Society

indicators.note: places the society beside the cutting, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: un is French for a
paring is cutting back or trimming

explanation.surface: A ruthless French society is slashing its budget.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsparing describes someone showing no mercy or leniency, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: In America, Joe's medical officer's useful device?

parts.note: GI Joe is the American private soldier, so a Joe belonging to the US army is a GI
MO is the abbreviation for medical officer

explanation.surface: An American soldier's army doctor carries a handy gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo is an informal word for a gadget, any handy mechanical contrivance.

clue.text: Appetizer produced by ancient city in Alpine region

indicators.note: the city is placed inside the region

parts.note: Savoy is a historic region in the French Alps
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A starter is made in a mountain area from an old town's recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury is a small salty dish, served as an appetizer or after dessert.

clue.text: Bonehead taking boiled pudding with hesitation

parts.note: a duff is a boiled or steamed suet pudding, as in plum duff
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A dimwit hesitates before tucking into a steamed pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A duffer is an incompetent or stupid person, much like a bonehead.

clue.text: Trendy group surrounding opener in county cricket, perhaps

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: the group goes round the letter that follows

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fashionable crowd gathers round the opening batsman in a county cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'county cricket' reads as one phrase; the definition is the insect called cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is a chirping insect, so cricket is an example of an insect.

clue.text: Overjoyed, seeing part-song almost complete

parts.note: a glee is an unaccompanied song for several voices

indicators.note: nearly all the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled at nearly finishing a choral piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleeful means full of delight, so it is a synonym of overjoyed.

clue.text: Note included in Conservative party's statement of beliefs

indicators.note: the note is put inside the other letters

parts.note: a do is a party
re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A footnote is added to the Conservative manifesto.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a formal statement of what someone believes.

clue.text: Solitary-sounding nurse, perhaps — one making costly advances!

indicators.note: signals that a word is taken for how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: lone means solitary
the nurse shark is one kind of shark

explanation.surface: A lonely-sounding nurse is a predatory moneylender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurse' suggests a carer in a hospital, but it is a species of shark.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan shark lends money at extortionate rates of interest, so his advances are costly.

clue.text: Liberal's berated gangster about formative years

indicators.note: the scolding word goes round the Liberal

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to berate
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
hood, short for hoodlum, is a gangster

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician scolded a mobster about his upbringing.
explanation.definitionFit: Childhood is the early period of life when character is formed.

clue.text: Justification one needed after jumping bail

indicators.note: the one comes after the shuffled letters
the word bail is made to jump about into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who skipped bail now needs an excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is an excuse or plea in defence, a justification.

clue.text: Eg Walton's fury about Sitwell, ultimately

indicators.note: the fury surrounds the letter that follows

parts.note: anger is fury

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Izaak Walton is furious about Edith Sitwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walton's' reads as 'Walton is'. Izaak Walton wrote The Compleat Angler; the Sitwells were a literary family.
explanation.definitionFit: Izaak Walton, author of The Compleat Angler, is the classic example of a fisherman.

clue.text: Is he Shakespearean fairy? No, gigantic beast!

parts.note: is is a form of the verb be
taken as written
Moth is a fairy in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a creature is one of Shakespeare's fairies and is told it is a huge monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Behemoth is the enormous biblical beast in Job, hence any huge creature.

clue.text: Noble make of car on seagoing vessel

parts.note: a marque is a make of car
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An aristocrat parks his fancy car aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquess is a nobleman ranking above an earl and below a duke.

clue.text: Intelligence required to take in new parts of speech

indicators.note: the intelligence word takes the letter inside itself

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence

explanation.surface: It takes brains to learn some new grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Nouns are a class of words, one of the traditional parts of speech.

clue.text: Dog unit Marie organised with daughter in south coast resort

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a new order
the daughter is placed inside the resort

parts.note: Poole is a seaside town in Dorset on England's south coast

explanation.surface: Marie and her daughter's group sort themselves out on holiday at the seaside with the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature poodle is a small breed of dog.

clue.text: Cancel university charge over in transatlantic city

indicators.note: these letters go inside the city

parts.note: NY is New York, across the Atlantic from Britain

indicators.note: in a down clue over turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: to fill is to charge, as a glass

explanation.surface: Tuition charges are being cancelled at a university in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify is to make void, which is to cancel.

clue.text: Former province's fruitless condition?

explanation.surface: A former South African province was in a state of having no fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, a state free of oranges is a fruitless one; 's links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orange Free State was a Boer republic, later a province of South Africa until 1994.

clue.text: Reserve novel librarians filed initially here?

definitions.text: Reserve novel librarians filed initially here?

parts.note: to book is to reserve
She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: the opening letters of each of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Booking a novel that librarians shelve here.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a place where librarians file novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Books are filed on a bookshelf.

clue.text: Antiseptic my lot distributed around hospital

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the hospital letter
the letters are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: My batch of disinfectant was handed out round the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' gives TYMOL, which 'around' wraps round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Thymol is a compound from thyme oil used as an antiseptic.

clue.text: Having ears pulled?

explanation.surface: Someone has had their ears tugged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lugs are ears in informal speech, so lugged means eared; to lug is also to drag.

clue.text: Cleric taking piece of jewellery, say, for overlaying

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard, not written

parts.note: an earring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A clergyman puts on a piece of jewellery as a covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneering is covering a surface with a thin layer, which is overlaying.

clue.text: Like one of the lads, terribly bolshie about last bit of work

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the next letter
the word is badly mangled into a new order
the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: One of the lads is very awkward about finishing his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns BOLSHIE into BLOEISH, which goes round K. Bolshie is British slang for awkward or rebellious.
explanation.definitionFit: Blokeish means typical of an ordinary man, matey and laddish.

clue.text: Candle-maker in trouble at first over permit?

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the letter above, so before, the next piece
the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to allow is to permit

explanation.surface: A candle-maker is in trouble initially about a licence.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat from which candles were made.

clue.text: Bigwig ready in Pretoria to visit key Europeans?

indicators.note: the money goes in among the other letters, as a visitor goes into a house

parts.note: G is a musical key
E is the abbreviation for European, so two of them give EE
ready is slang for cash, and the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A dignitary ready in Pretoria visits important Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' as a noun is cash, as in 'readies'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a person of high rank or importance, a bigwig.

clue.text: First-class accountants climbing tree

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the letters upwards, backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
CA is a chartered accountant, so two make accountants

explanation.surface: Top accountants are climbing a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns AICACA upwards into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a tree or shrub, also called wattle.

clue.text: A Russian fighter supported by old pal in Buenos Aires?

indicators.note: in a down clue the support goes beneath, so after

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter plane

explanation.surface: A Russian jet is backed by an old friend in Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, and Spanish is spoken in Buenos Aires.
